newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Strikes to cost South Korea $1 billion by year end.
newsitem.headline: Strikes to cost South Korea $1 billion by year end.

text.p: Strikes that have crippled much of South Korean industry will cost the country more than $1 billion in lost production by the end of the year, the trade ministry said on Saturday.
The ministry put the figure in local currency at 911 billion won.
Production lost through previous industrial action this year was estimated at 2.7 trillion won ($3.2 billion), ministry official Choi Tae-hwan said.
The statement estimated current strikes would cost $357 million in lost exports by the end of the year on top of $387 million in overseas sales already lost this year.
Strikes began on Thursday after the government rammed through a controversial labour law in a clandestine dawn session of the National Assembly.
